chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْه، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنِ النَّدْرِ بْنِ سَوَيْد، عَنْ يَحْيَى الْحَلَبِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from his father Imran ibn Ali who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ أَبَا الْخَطَّابِ وَلَعَنَ مَنْ قُتِلَ مَعَهُ وَلَعَنَ مَنْ بَقِيَ مِنْهُمْ وَلَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ دَخَلَ قَلْبَهُ رَحْمَةٌ لَهُمْ

translations.en: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: May Allah curse Abu al-Khattab, and may He curse those who were killed with him, and may He curse those who remained from them, and may Allah curse the one to whose heart enters mercy for them.

en.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) pronounces a curse upon Abu al-Khattab (Hafs ibn al-Sayyab) and his companions who were killed alongside him, as well as those who survived. He further curses anyone whose heart develops mercy or affection for them, highlighting the theological significance of their betrayal and the emotional state of their followers. This narration underscores the Shia concept of *al-wala' wa al-barra'* (affiliation and disaffiliation), emphasizing that loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt requires not only rejecting their enemies but also maintaining a spiritual aversion to their enduring legacy.
en.seo_question: Who did Imam al-Sadiq curse regarding Abu al-Khattab and his companions?

key_terms.أَبُو الْخَطَّابِ: Abu al-Khattab (Hafs ibn al-Sayyab), a companion of Imam al-Sadiq known for his betrayal.
key_terms.لَعَنَ اللَّهُ: May Allah curse (a formula of divine condemnation).
key_terms.رَحْمَةٌ: Mercy or affection (in the context of the heart's attachment to the cursed).
